text:
oliver: hi all, first-day snag. VPN (WireGuard newhire-prod) shows connected but `git clone` and `curl https://api.internal.redwood.internal` hang or are painfully slow. Browser to intranet sometimes loads but large downloads fail. Anyone seen this? :grimacing:

it-ops: welcome! quick question: do small requests succeed but large transfers fail? sounds like an MTU/MSS issue over the VPN. Can you paste `wg show` and a short `curl -v` output? Also which OS?

oliver: I'm on macOS Ventura. `wg show` shows `mtu: 1420` actually, but I didn't set it. curl -v just hangs after TCP handshake sometimes:```* Connected to api.internal.redwood.internal (10.10.8.9) port 443 (#0)
* found 0 certificates in /etc/ssl/cert.pem
* ALPN, offering h2
* Cipher selection: ...
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished (some seconds pass)
(then stalls and eventually times out)```

neteng: thanks. can you run a quick tcpdump while reproducing the curl? `sudo tcpdump -i utun3 -n tcp and host 10.10.8.9 and port 443 -w /tmp/vpn.pcap` then stop after a few seconds and `tcpdump -r /tmp/vpn.pcap -nn` to look for retransmits and 'fragmentation needed' ICMPs. If you can't share pcap, look for lots of retransmits or repeated SYNs.

oliver: tcpdump shows lots of `[TCP Retransmission]` and occasional `ICMP destination unreachable, fragmentation needed and DF set` messages. So probably PMTU issue.

it-ops: yup that's PMTU. Common on consumer ISPs or carriers that don't handle large encapsulated packets. Two quick fixes: 1) Lower the MTU for the WireGuard interface (macOS): `sudo ifconfig utun3 mtu 1280` (test-only). 2) On Linux or managed gateways, add MSS clamping in PostUp so TCP connections clamp to path MTU:```PostUp = /sbin/iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu```and PostDown to remove it.

jamie: adding specifics for laptop OSes:
- macOS (test): `sudo ifconfig <utunX> mtu 1280` then retry downloads. To make persistent with our WireGuard client, add `MTU = 1280` in the peer config or ask IT to push updated profile.
- Linux: add the PostUp/PostDown iptables mangle TCPMSS commands in `/etc/wireguard/wg0.conf` so the gateway clamps MSS for forwarded traffic. Example:```[Interface]
Address = 10.10.4.12/32
PostUp = /sbin/iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
PostDown = /sbin/iptables -t mangle -D FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu```
- Windows: change MTU on the adapter with `netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "Ethernet" mtu=1280 store=persistent` (replace adapter name) or use vendor docs.

oliver: set `sudo ifconfig utun3 mtu 1280` and retried `git clone` — it finished fast. :tada: Thanks!

it-ops: great. we'll update the onboarding notes: push MTU=1280 in the client profile as fallback and add TCPMSS PostUp on gateways. Jamie, can you open a ticket to standardize this for managed profiles?

jamie: will do. Also adding a short diagnostic snippet to the docs:```# check for PMTU issues
sudo tcpdump -i <vpn_iface> -n tcp and port 443 -c 50
# look for "fragmentation needed" or retransmits in the output
```

devex-bot: created ticket #INFR-4257 to add MTU/TCPMSS guidance and a one-liner diagnostic to the new-hire VPN onboarding doc.

oliver: leaving this note for other new-hires: if big downloads / git hang over VPN, try lowering the WireGuard MTU or ask infra to enable MSS clamping on the gateway. saved my first-day dev flow. :relieved:
